Definition: from G2532 and G1564; likewise from that place (or time):--and afterward (from) (thence), thence also.
BiblicalUsage: Kakeithen is 'and from there' — the travelling word of Acts. From there God gave Israel a king; from there Paul and Barnabas sailed back to Antioch; from there they came the next day to Miletus, on the road to Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Luke's 'from there' shows the gospel moving: it never stayed where it started, and neither should I.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
